entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Donatien Mahele Lieko Bokungu was a prominent Zairean general who served as the last army chief during the long reign of Mobutu Sese Seko.

Born in the Belgian Congo, Lieko Bokungu's rise to power was influenced by the Zairean government's efforts to maintain control over the country's vast mineral resources. His appointment as army chief in 1978 marked a turning point in the regime's efforts to suppress opposition and maintain its grip on power.

Lieko Bokungu's legacy is complex and multifaceted. He played a key role in the Zairean government's efforts to modernize the country's military, but his tenure was also marked by allegations of human rights abuses and repression of dissent. His death in 1997 came at a time when the Zairean government was facing increased international pressure to reform and democratize.

Despite his controversial legacy, Lieko Bokungu remains an important figure in Zairean history, representing the intersection of local politics and global events. His story serves as a reminder of the complexities of power and the ongoing struggles for democracy and human rights in Africa.
